note: Verilog logical shifts toward VHDL, and the design that found hif-backend#94. hif2vhdl routed the operand through to_integer and then applied `sll` to the result, producing VHDL that was invalid twice over: to_unsigned was called with a single std_logic_vector where numeric_std declares (natural, natural), and sll was applied to an integer where VHDL defines it on array types. vhdl2hif accepts the file and exits 0 - so reparsing is not evidence the VHDL is well formed - and hif2verilog then aborted in getBestCandidate, unable to resolve the call. It now writes `std_logic_vector(unsigned(a) sll to_integer(unsigned(n)))`, and the excursion through VHDL and back preserves behaviour. Both shift directions are in one fixture because they are one lowering and one defect. Distinct from combinational/shifter.v, a bare .v on plain_roundtrip whose question is whether regenerated Verilog reparses.
